comments.author: @matthewcampbell7286
comments.text:
Mike’s inference loop idea is something that been tried. It sort of the core of all Agent swarm ideas. But it underestimates how errors snowball. Having the model “self-prompt and loop” can produce reasonable output for a few rounds, but as soon as it makes a logical mistake or adopts a false premise, that flawed token stays in the sliding context window and keeps driving every subsequent step. Reflection or revision prompts may temporarily suppress the error, but attention simply renormalizes over all tokens, New corrective tokens lose weight, while the original bad token remains entrenched. Vanilla transformers have no built-in way to forget or overwrite mistakes, so without grounding mechanisms like mixed teacher forcing, noise injection during training, or memory augmented architectures, the model just rebuilds its house of cards.

Just to be clear this is fixable.... but the work still being done on it
